newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rebound to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rebound to new record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended above the 5,100-point market for the first time ever on Monday and chalked up their first record close of the month, as investors shopped for bargains after an early dip.
"The market began to buy ahead of third-quarter earnings, on the perception the second quarter gave a taste of better things to come," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage.

The blue-chip IPC share index closed up 68.21 points, or 1.35 percent, at an all-time high of 5,135.24, after falling as low as 5,023.15 in mid-morning trade. The previous record of 5,067.83 was set last Thursday.
"Many players have been rearranging portfolios in recent days, which did lead to some consolidation, but they came back today and shares rallied again," Copca added.
Dealers said buying was selective rather than widespread, but had a heavy impact amid relatively light volume of 93.3 million shares traded.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced decliners by 66 to 37 out of 125 stocks that changed hands.
"We did see money flow into the bourse today, but nowhere near as much as last week, and volume was well down, too," a floor trader said.

Financial group Bancomer was the most active stock of the day, and accounted for more than one quarter of all shares traded. The group's A shares gained 22 centavos (3 cents) to 3.42 pesos (44 cents), to close the gap with the B shares, dealers said.
Bancomer B series meanwhile rebounded from an early slide to end up 2 centavos (less than 1 cent) at 5.60 pesos (72 cents) on portfolio buying, dealers added.

Market heavyweight Telmex also recovered on bargain-hunting to close up 15 centavos (2 cents) at 21.75 pesos ($2.78), a record in peso terms. The telecommunications stock's American Depositary Receipts gained 3/8 to 55-7/16 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"Some stocks missed the party," a desk trader said. "Dealers took profits all day on Carso and Cifra."
Conglomerate Grupo Carso shed 40 centavos (5 cents) to 62.00 pesos ($7.93), while retailer Cifra ended off 4 centavos (0.5 cent) at 14.98 pesos ($1.92).
